### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

Target object, stated in the first breath: *"a six hundred and fifty dollar hold from the demo skis
she hired at Silverpine is still sitting against her card … she would like somebody to deal with
it."* So the object is the security hold on one Equipment Rental and Demo agreement, and the asked-for
outcome is that the hold be dealt with.

Identification: she volunteers name **Marta Sandoval-Reyes** and mobile **3035550318**; on request
date of birth **1979-06-14**; only if asked, passholder number **GR43005512**, postal code **84109**,
email **marta.sandovalreyes@northgatemail.com**.

Timing she supplies: collected the skis on **26 January**; written down to come back on the Sunday;
mid-week she rang the shop about keeping them a day longer and *"was told it would have to go in as a
request and be looked at, and nobody ever came back to her"*; she and her sister had a slopeside
studio that week; she drove home on **2 February**; she is sure the skis went back on the Saturday
but *"would have to look at her photographs if anyone needs the date confirmed, and she will not
invent one"*.

Boundary and authorisation: she is passive throughout. *"Asked anything the collective's own records
would answer instead … she says plainly that she has no idea and the agent will have to look."*
*"Whenever the agent explains that something on the hire has to be settled first, she takes it
without argument and tells them to go ahead"* — i.e. she authorises the agent's own service writes.
*"If the agent then tells her money is still outstanding on the hire and asks her to clear it, she
says that is fine and pays it herself with the card in her hand, running whatever the agent passes
over to her"* — i.e. she will execute a **user-owned** tool the agent unlocks and hands over, but only
at the agent's direction. She offers no figure and disputes none. She rings off once told the hold is
dealt with **and how much is going back**.

So: the simulator conveys a need, answers passively, and runs one handed-over user tool. It never
names a policy, a tool, an amount or an order. The **amount going back** is the one figure she
expects to be told.

### 2. Act now, wait, or refuse — and the visible eligibility grounds

**Act now.** Every gate the visible documents impose is already met at 2027-02-09 10:40 MST.

Records reached by tool (`find_rental_agreements{customer_id}`), agreement
`8b1f61d2-3de3-43b4-9da4-3b3e38bd9e78`:
`variant_name='Demo Ski & Board Rental'`, `status='returned'`, `season_code='2026-27'`,
`pickup_date='2027-01-26'`, `due_date='2027-01-31'`, `returned_date='2027-02-06'`,
`reserved_date='2026-12-18'`, `rental_days_booked=6`, `rental_days_remaining=0`,
`item_serial='DEMO4471KX'`, `damage_waiver_taken=True`, `damage_deposit_usd=650.0`,
`rental_balance_usd=65.0`, `swap_count=1`, `signed_release_on_file=True`.

Eligibility grounds actually used:

- *Security Holds and Damage Found on Returned Equipment Rental and Demo Kit* §4: **"A hold is
  released only while the agreement stands in the overdue, returned, cancelled or uncollected
  state."** The agreement stands `returned`. Its table gives `returned → Hold may be released: yes`.
- Same §4: **"The hold is released no later than the package's release period counted in business
  days from the day the kit was handed in."** *Finance Office Schedule …* gives the Demo package a
  hold release period of **7 business days**. Hand-in 2027-02-06 (Saturday); business days counted
  with the anchor as day zero and Saturdays/Sundays excluded — so day zero is 2027-02-06, and the
  period has certainly not expired by 2027-02-09 (Tuesday). The release is inside the period, i.e.
  not late, and in any event the document sets a *deadline*, not a waiting period: nothing in it
  makes the release premature.
- *Kit Out Beyond the Date Written on an Equipment Rental and Demo Agreement*, "Which agreements can
  carry a fee": **"A fee is raised against an agreement only while the agreement stands in the
  confirmed, picked up, overdue, returned, cancelled or uncollected state."** `returned` is in the
  list, so the shop fee for the late hand-in may still be raised now.
- *Putting a Figure on a Technician's Finding Against Equipment Rental and Demo Kit*: **"A finding
  entered when kit was checked back in stands on the agreement's rental account at nil until it is
  assessed."** The account carries exactly such a finding (below), so the assessment is available now.

Nothing on the visible surface points at refusal or a handoff: the request is squarely inside the
rentals charter, and none of the uncovered grounds the blueprint lists (waiving an assessed charge on
the guest's word, releasing a hold before the kit is back, hiring outside the fitting range,
injury/quality claims) is raised.

*Residual tension noted, not treated as blocking (see §7).* *The Basis on Which Equipment Rental and
Demo Hire Is Charged*, "The standing of the agreement", says **"A charge is raised against an
agreement only while the agreement stands in the reserved, confirmed, picked up or overdue state"**
and tables `returned → no`. Read at its widest that sentence would forbid both writes above on this
`returned` agreement — and would make *any* damage assessment impossible, since an assessment is by
construction made on handed-in kit. Read by specificity (that document governs how *hire* is charged;
the fee document and the damage document each state their own standing) both writes stand. I take the
specific reading, and record the width of the wording as a point to test against the source.

### 4. Each scored parameter: formula in words, inputs, intermediates, result

Four figures are decided, in this order. For each I give the baseline the computation document alone
yields, then every tiered rule the visible documents state for one of its inputs, the tier this
customer is on, and the query return that puts them there.

#### (a) The shop's fee for kit handed in after its date — **249.08 USD**

Computation document: *Working Out the Shop's Fee for Late-Returned Equipment Rental and Demo Kit*.
Its own words: **"The stretch is counted from the day after the date written on the agreement through
the date the kit reached the counter inclusive"**; **"No day of the stretch is set aside"**; **"The
daily figure … is the package's own daily late fee"**; **"The daily figure is taken in full, without
the household's standing with the collective weighed against it"**; **"The daily figure carries no
uplift for what the collective has at stake in the kit"**; **"The share and the uplift act on the
daily figure itself rather than on one another's results, and neither is rounded before the fee is
worked out"**; **"the number of days in the stretch multiplied by the daily figure … worked out once
at the end and rounded half up to two decimal places"**; **"The fee is never more than the package's
replacement value."**

Tiered rules found from the records, and the tier this customer is on:

1. *Where the Stretch of Overdue Days Begins on an Equipment Rental and Demo Agreement* — **"Where
   the shop holds a request on the agreement to keep the kit to a later date, the stretch is counted
   from the day after the date the guest asked the kit to be kept to, through the date the kit
   reached the counter inclusive."** Reached from the words on the record: `find_rental_service_requests`
   returns `request_type='extension'`, `requested_due_date='2027-02-01'`. The rule reads the request
   whatever it came to — its own point of judgement says only *"The request read is the one standing
   on that agreement asking for the kit to be kept to a later date, and the date read from it is the
   date the guest asked the kit to be kept to"* — so `outcome='declined'` does not take it out of the
   first row. Stretch = **2027-02-02 through 2027-02-06 inclusive = 5 days**.
2. *Days Set Aside From an Overdue Stretch … Where the Household Is Staying With the Collective* —
   **"Where the household holds a Resort Lodging reservation for the season whose departure date
   falls after the date written on the agreement, the days from the day after the date written on the
   agreement through that departure date are set aside."** Reached from the lodging row's own words
   (`departure_date='2027-02-02'`, `season_code='2026-27'`). 2027-02-02 falls after 2027-01-31, so
   2027-02-01 and 2027-02-02 are set aside = **2 days**.
   Stretch after the set-aside: 5 − 2 = **3 days**.
3. *The Daily Figure on Advance-Booked Equipment Rental and Demo Agreements Handed In Late* —
   **"Where the agreement was recorded at least the package's advance booking period in days before
   the collection date, and it runs for at least the package's multi-day threshold in days, the daily
   figure is the package's multi-day day rate raised by the late hand-in uplift … The late hand-in
   uplift is 35 per cent."** Reached from `reserved_date='2026-12-18'` against
   `pickup_date='2027-01-26'` — a lead of 39 days, against the Demo package's advance booking period
   of **10 days** and multi-day threshold of **2 days** (both tabled in that document, and again on
   *Reductions Held Against the Equipment Rental and Demo Packages* and the rate card). The agreement
   runs 6 days. Daily figure = **82.00 × 1.35 = 110.70 USD** (the document's own table gives the Demo
   multi-day day rate as 82.00 USD).
4. *The Household's Standing With the Collective and the Daily Figure on Late Equipment Rental and
   Demo Kit* — **"Where the household holds a Season Pass Programme pass standing active for the
   season, and the pass account carries at least 8 lift scans in the four months before the fee is
   worked out, the daily figure is taken at the regular skier share of itself. The regular skier
   share is 55 per cent."** Reached from the pass row (`status='active'`, `season_code='2026-27'`) and
   the 11 scans inside 2026-10-09 … 2027-02-09. Share = **55 per cent**.
5. *What the Collective Has at Stake in Late Equipment Rental and Demo Kit* — **"Where the security
   hold standing against the agreement is at or above 500.00 USD, the daily figure is raised by the
   high exposure uplift. The high exposure uplift is 20 per cent."** Reached from the
   `rentals_deposit_hold` row of 650.00 USD with no release row against it; the document's point of
   judgement defines the hold standing as *"what was placed against it less what has already gone
   back"* = **650.00 USD**. Uplift = **20 per cent**.

Because the share and the uplift each act on the daily figure itself and never on one another's
results, each contributes its own movement measured against 110.70: 110.70 × (0.55 + 0.20) =
**83.025 USD a day**, unrounded as the document requires.

Fee = 3 × 83.025 = 249.075 → rounded half up to two decimal places = **249.08 USD**. Ceiling check:
the Demo replacement value is 1650.00 USD, so the ceiling does not bite.

#### (b) The amount the guest bears for the technician's finding — **61.00 USD**

Computation document: *Bench Standard: the Amount a Guest Bears for a Damage Finding on Equipment
Rental and Demo Kit*. Its own words: first step **"the heavy use share of the package's replacement
value … The heavy use share is 10 per cent"**; **"Nothing is set aside for the kit having been taken
out of the shop's sight. Nothing is set aside for a technician having had the kit in hand part-way
through the hire. Each set-aside share acts on the amount left after the step before it, and the
amount left is rounded half up to two decimal places at each of those steps"**; **"The whole of what
is then left is carried to the cover step"**; **"The guest bears the full cover share of the amount
left. The full cover share is 25 per cent"**; **"The figure the guest bears is taken as it stands,
rounded half up to two decimal places"** and is never below zero. The Demo replacement value is
**1650.00 USD** (*Finance Office Schedule of Security Holds, Waivers and Replacement Values*).

Tiered rules found from the records:

1. *Dates Out and the Share a Damage Finding Carries on Equipment Rental and Demo Kit* — **"Where
   that account carries at least 4 such dates but fewer than 8, the amount the finding carries is the
   moderate use share of that replacement value instead"**, 16 per cent. Reached from the six
   `rentals_day_consume` rows. → 0.16 × 1650.00 = **264.00 USD**.
2. *Delivered Equipment Rental and Demo Kit and the Allowance Set Aside From a Finding* — **"Where
   the agreement's rental account carries the package's delivery charge against the agreement, and
   the household holds a Resort Lodging reservation for the season, the delivered set-aside share of
   the amount is set aside. The delivered set-aside share is 20 per cent."** Reached from the
   `charge_category='delivery_fee'` row of 65.00 USD (the Demo delivery price on *What Is Handed Over
   With Each … Package* is 65.00 USD) and the Slopeside Studio reservation for 2026-27. → 52.80 set
   aside, leaving **211.20 USD**.
3. *Kit Changed Part-Way Through an Equipment Rental and Demo Hire: the Allowance Set Aside From a
   Finding* — **"Where the agreement shows the kit was changed for another model once, and the rental
   account carries at least 4 dates the item now on the agreement was out, the once changed set-aside
   share is set aside instead. The once changed set-aside share is 15 per cent."** Reached from
   `swap_count=1` on the agreement and the 4 day-consume rows carrying `item_serial='DEMO4471KX'`,
   which is the agreement's `item_serial`. → 31.68 set aside, leaving **179.52 USD**.
4. *Households Taught by the Snowsports School and the Amount Carried Forward From an Equipment
   Rental and Demo Finding* — **"Where the household holds a Snowsports School booking for the
   season, and the school account carries at least 3 sessions delivered in the four months before the
   assessment is made, the school heavy share of what is left is carried forward. The school heavy
   share is 70 per cent."** Reached from the lesson booking for 2026-27 and the three
   `lessons_session_deliver` rows of 2027-01-27/28/29. → 179.52 × 0.70 = **125.664 USD** carried.
5. *The Damage Waiver and the Share of an Equipment Rental and Demo Finding Borne by the Guest* —
   **"Where the waiver was taken, but the rental account carries the waiver charged for fewer dates
   than that account shows the kit was out, the guest bears the partial cover share of the amount
   left instead. The partial cover share is 60 per cent."** Reached from `damage_waiver_taken=True`
   and the `charge_category='damage_waiver'` row whose `quantity` is **4**, against **6** dates the
   kit was out. → 125.664 × 0.60 = **75.3984 USD**.
6. *The Gap Between Hand-In and Assessment on an Equipment Rental and Demo Finding* — **"Where the
   kit reached the counter more than 2 days before the assessment is made but no more than 7 days
   before it, the figure the guest bears is taken at the recent look share of itself and carried up
   to the whole dollar above. The recent look share is 80 per cent."** Reached from
   `returned_date='2027-02-06'` against the assessment made today, 2027-02-09 — a gap of **3 days**,
   which the document's band table puts in the 3–7 row. → 75.3984 × 0.80 = 60.31872 → carried up to
   the whole dollar above = **61.00 USD**.

#### (c) The amount the guest is asked to hand over at the counter — **150.08 USD**

Computation document: *The Figure the Counter Asks For on an Equipment Rental and Demo Agreement*.
Its own words: **"The whole of what still stands on the agreement, namely the hire rate and the
add-ons raised on it together with the shop fees and the assessments raised on it, less the money
already collected against it, is taken at the counter"**; **"Nothing is set against what is taken from
resort credit"**; **"Nothing is written off for the shop's own part in the hire"**; **"Nothing is
left standing against the security hold"**; **"The credit set against what is taken, the allowance
written off and the amount left standing against the hold are each taken off the figure the counter
step arrived at, and none of them acts on another's result"**; **"never below zero, and rounded half
up to two decimal places at that last step only"**.

Tiered rules found from the records:

1. *What Is Taken at the Counter and What Is Left Standing on an Equipment Rental and Demo Agreement*
   — **"Where the household holds a Resort Lodging reservation for the season, only the shop fees and
   the assessments raised on the agreement are taken at the counter, and what is left of the hire rate
   stands on the agreement to be collected another day."** Reached from the Slopeside Studio row for
   2026-27; the rule's own table says the lodging row governs *"whether or not money has already been
   collected"*. Counter step = 249.08 + 61.00 = **310.08 USD**.
2. *Resort Credit Standing on the Household's Pass Account Set Against an Equipment Rental and Demo
   Settlement* — **"Where the household holds a Season Pass Programme pass standing active for the
   season, and the pass account carries resort credit issued and not yet drawn, the whole of that
   credit standing is set against what is taken."** Reached from the active pass and the single
   `passes_credit_issue` row of 85.00 USD with no draw against it (the pass row's own
   `pass_credit_usd` is 85.0). → **85.00 USD**.
3. *The Goodwill Allowance Written Off an Equipment Rental and Demo Settlement* — **"Where the shop
   holds a request raised on the agreement, and the rental account carries at least 5 dates the kit
   was out, the service goodwill allowance is written off what is taken. The service goodwill
   allowance is 25.00 USD."** Reached from the one rental service request on the agreement and the 6
   dates out; its point of judgement says *"Any request standing raised on that agreement opens the
   allowance; what the request was for does not narrow it."* → **25.00 USD**.
4. *Assessments Left Standing Against the Security Hold on an Equipment Rental and Demo Agreement* —
   **"Where the rental account carries an assessment raised against the agreement, and the security
   hold standing against it is at or above that assessment, the assessment is left standing against
   that hold up to the deferral cap. The deferral cap is 50.00 USD."** Reached from the assessment
   just written (61.00 USD) against a hold standing of 650.00 USD. → **50.00 USD**.

Amount = 310.08 − 85.00 − 25.00 − 50.00 = **150.08 USD**, above zero, rounded once.

#### (d) What goes back from the security hold — **628.00 USD**, entry `partially_forfeited`

Computation document: *Arriving at What Goes Back From the Security Hold on an Equipment Rental and
Demo Agreement*. Its own words: **"What the agreement still owes is the hire rate, the shop fees and
the assessments raised on it less the money collected against it, rounded half up to two decimal
places, and it is never below zero"**; **"Nothing of what the agreement still owes is moved to a
lodging folio"**; **"Nothing of what the agreement still owes is met by a protection plan"**; **"What
is moved to a folio and what is met by a protection plan are both taken off what the agreement still
owes before the multiple is applied"**; **"The amount kept back is what is then left taken once over,
that is at the clean retention multiple of 100 per cent"**; **"Nothing is released back to the
household on its standing … The allowance is taken off the amount kept back after the multiple has
been applied"**; **"The amount kept back is taken to the cent"**; **"What goes back to the guest is
the security hold standing less the amount kept back, never below zero"**; and **"Where the whole of
the hold standing goes back the entry is recorded as released, where part of it is kept back the
entry is recorded as partially forfeited, and where none of it goes back the entry is recorded as
forfeited."**

By the time this is worked, the account carries: charges 315.50 + 60.00 + 65.00 + 249.08 + 61.00 =
750.58 USD, money collected 375.50 + 150.08 = 525.58 USD. **What the agreement still owes = 225.00
USD** — which is also what the agreement's own running figure comes to (65.00 + 61.00 + 249.08 −
150.08), the two agreeing exactly.

Tiered rules found from the records:

1. *Moving What an Equipment Rental and Demo Agreement Still Owes on to a Lodging Folio* — **"Where
   the household holds a Resort Lodging reservation for the season standing checked out whose folio
   carries nothing still to be collected, what is moved to that folio is capped at the folio transfer
   cap. The folio transfer cap is 120.00 USD."** Reached from `status='checked_out'` and
   `folio_balance_usd=0.0` (its point of judgement: *"A folio carrying nothing still to be collected
   includes one standing at nil"*). → **120.00 USD**.
2. *Protection Cover Met Against What an Equipment Rental and Demo Agreement Still Owes* — **"Where
   the household holds a Pass and Trip Protection plan standing active written over the agreement,
   whose cover left is below what the agreement still owes, the cover left on it is met by that
   plan."** Reached from the protection plan whose `covered_holding_id` is this `rental_id`,
   `status='active'`, `benefit_remaining_usd=40.0`. → **40.00 USD**.
   Left before the multiple: 225.00 − 120.00 − 40.00 = **65.00 USD**.
3. *The Margin Kept Back on Open and Assessed Equipment Rental and Demo Agreements* — **"Where the
   rental account carries an assessment against an item on the agreement, and the agreement stands
   with the kit handed in, the amount kept back is the assessed retention multiple of what is then
   left. The assessed retention multiple is 125 per cent."** Reached from `status='returned'` and the
   assessment now standing at 61.00 USD. → 65.00 × 1.25 = **81.25 USD**.
4. *The Standing Allowance Released Back on an Equipment Rental and Demo Security Hold* — **"Where
   the household holds a Season Pass Programme pass standing active for the season, and the pass
   account shows nothing still to be collected on its instalments, the clean standing allowance is
   released back and taken off the amount kept back. The clean standing allowance is 60.00 USD."**
   Reached from the active pass with `installment_balance_usd=0.0`. → 81.25 − 60.00 = **21.25 USD**.
5. *How Long Equipment Rental and Demo Kit Has Been Back, and How the Amount Kept Back Is Taken* —
   **"Where the kit reached the counter at least 2 days before the hold is settled, and the rental
   account carries more than one payment collected against the agreement, the amount kept back is
   carried up to the whole dollar above."** Reached from `returned_date='2027-02-06'` against today
   (a gap of 3 days) and the two payment rows that stand once the counter settlement has been taken
   (the 2026-12-18 payment of 375.50 USD and the new one). → 21.25 carried up to **22.00 USD**.

What goes back = 650.00 − 22.00 = **628.00 USD**. Part of the hold is kept, so `deposit_status` is
**`partially_forfeited`**.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**Problems, and the direction of the dependencies**

```
release the security hold            (the only thing the customer named)
  └─ take the counter settlement     (waited on by the release)
       ├─ assess the technician's finding   (waited on by the counter settlement)
       └─ raise the shop's late hand-in fee (waited on by the counter settlement)
```

**Handling order:** assess the finding and raise the late fee (either order) → take the counter
settlement → release the hold.

**Hop 1 — the hold release waits on the money collected standing against the charges raised.**
*Giving Back the Security Hold on an Equipment Rental and Demo Agreement* states, in the blocked
policy's own document: **"What goes back to the guest is worked out only after the money collected
against the agreement stands against the charges raised on it."** That names a **state** of the
record, not an act. Query: the ledger shows charges of 440.50 USD and one payment of 375.50 USD,
leaving 65.00 USD — the agreement's own `rental_balance_usd`. So the state does not hold. Which write
brings it about? *Money Taken at the Counter Against an Equipment Rental and Demo Agreement* says of
itself: **"One entry books a single payment on the agreement's rental account for the amount the
guest hands over and lowers the amount still to be collected on the agreement by the same figure …
that entry is what the account then carries as money collected against the agreement."** That is the
only document in the corpus that describes a write producing "money collected against the agreement".
→ **state-derived.**

**Hop 2 — the counter settlement waits on every finding carrying the amount the guest bears.**
*Money Taken at the Counter…* states, in its own document: **"The amount the guest is asked to hand
over is fixed only after every finding a technician has entered against an item on the agreement
carries the amount the guest bears for it."** A state again. Query: the ledger carries a
`rentals_damage_charge` row dated 2027-02-06 whose `amount_usd` is **0.00** against
`item_serial='DEMO4471KX'`, `damage_code='binding_damage'`. Does that count as a finding that carries
no amount? *Putting a Figure on a Technician's Finding…* settles it in the words the record uses:
**"A finding entered when kit was checked back in stands on the agreement's rental account at nil
until it is assessed"**, and **"Writing the figure onto the finding raises the amount still to be
collected on the agreement by the same figure."** So the nil row is exactly an unassessed finding, and
that document describes the write that makes it carry an amount. → **state-derived.**

**Hop 3 — the counter settlement waits on the account carrying the shop fee for the days beyond the
date.** Same document: **"The amount the guest is asked to hand over is fixed only after the account
carries the shop fee owed for the days the kit stayed out beyond the date written on the agreement."**
A state. Query: the agreement's `due_date` is 2027-01-31 and its `returned_date` is 2027-02-06, so the
kit did stay out beyond the date; the ledger carries **no** fee row of any kind. Which write brings
the state about? *The Shop's Fee for Equipment Rental and Demo Kit Handed In After Its Date* —
**"Kit hired on an agreement … that reaches a shop counter after the date written on that agreement
carries the shop's fee for the days it stayed out"**, and **"One entry books a single late hand-in
fee on the agreement's rental account for the amount given and raises the amount still to be
collected on the agreement by the same figure."** → **state-derived.**

No hop was **pre-solved**. No document names another problem's tool, states a route between problems,
or aggregates the chain: each blocked document states only what its own result waits on, in the state
form, and the depended-on documents describe their own writes in the same words the records use
("money collected against the agreement", "stands … at nil until it is assessed", "the shop's fee for
the days it stayed out"). No hop was **action-named**.

### 7. Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported by the visible materials.** Every figure above traces to a
published sentence and a query return; nothing needed a hidden field. In particular, the two
independent routes to what the agreement still owes (charges-less-collected from the ledger rows, and
the agreement's own running `rental_balance_usd` walked forward) agree at 225.00 USD.

**The closest alternatives, and what excludes each:**

- *Release the hold now, without settling anything.* Excluded by the prerequisite sentence in the
  release document itself — **"worked out only after the money collected against the agreement stands
  against the charges raised on it"** — and by the ledger showing 65.00 USD uncollected before any of
  the writes.
- *Start the overdue stretch on 2027-02-01 (the day after the date written on the agreement).*
  Excluded by *Where the Stretch of Overdue Days Begins…* first row, which the extension request on
  the agreement opens: the stretch runs from the day after **2027-02-01**, the date the guest asked
  the kit to be kept to.
- *Read the request out of the first row because it was declined.* Excluded by that document's own
  point of judgement, which conditions only on a request *"standing on that agreement asking for the
  kit to be kept to a later date"* and reads from it only *"the date the guest asked the kit to be
  kept to"*.
- *Set aside only one travel day.* Excluded by the departure date 2027-02-02 falling **after** the
  date written on the agreement (2027-01-31), which is the first row of *Days Set Aside From an
  Overdue Stretch…*, not the travel-day row.
- *Charge the Demo daily late fee of 68.00 USD.* Excluded by *The Daily Figure on Advance-Booked …
  Agreements Handed In Late*, whose first row is opened by a 39-day lead against the Demo advance
  period of 10 days.
- *Compound the 55 per cent share and the 20 per cent uplift.* Excluded by the computation document's
  **"The share and the uplift act on the daily figure itself rather than on one another's results"**.
- *Count 6 dates out as the light-use band, or count only the 4 dates of the current item.* Excluded
  by *Dates Out and the Share a Damage Finding Carries…*, whose count is **"the dates the agreement's
  rental account carries for the kit being out"** — 6, in the 4–7 row — while the 4-date count belongs
  to a different rule (*Kit Changed Part-Way Through…*), which says in terms that what is counted
  there is **"the dates carried against the item that now stands on the agreement"**.
- *Take the full 100 per cent cover share because the waiver was taken.* Excluded by *The Damage
  Waiver and the Share…* middle row: the waiver row's `quantity` of 4 is fewer than the 6 dates out.
- *Take the counter figure over the whole balance.* Excluded by *What Is Taken at the Counter…* first
  row, opened by the lodging reservation for the season.
- *Cap the resort credit at 50.00 USD.* Excluded by the same document's note that **"The cap bites on
  the second row only"**, the second row being the one where no pass stands active.
- *Move the whole 225.00 USD to the folio.* Excluded by the folio carrying nothing still to be
  collected, which is the capped row.
- *Apply the protection plan's `covered_value_usd` of 1650.00.* Excluded by the protection document
  reading **"its cover left"**, which the plan row carries as `benefit_remaining_usd=40.0`.
- *Take the amount kept back to the cent (21.25).* Excluded by *How Long … Kit Has Been Back…* first
  row, opened by the 3-day gap and the two payments standing at that moment.
- *Record the entry as `released` or `forfeited`.* Excluded by the release computation's own
  sentence: part of the hold is kept back, so it is `partially_forfeited`.
- *Refuse or hand off.* Nothing visible supports it; every gate is met and the subject is inside the
  charter.

**Where the visible surface leaves something open, I have not closed it** — recorded as policy-side
notes, not as document defects:
- *The Basis on Which … Hire Is Charged* says a charge may be raised only in reserved/confirmed/
  picked up/overdue, while *Kit Out Beyond the Date…* lets a **fee** be raised on a `returned`
  agreement and the damage documents describe assessments made on handed-in kit. The two are
  reconciled by specificity and by the fact that the wide reading would make every damage assessment
  impossible, but the wide sentence is on the visible surface and is flagged for the source check.
- The release computation names **"the hire rate, the shop fees and the assessments"** where the
  counter computation names **"the hire rate and the add-ons raised on it together with the shop fees
  and the assessments"**. I read the two as the same set (the agreement's own running figure confirms
  the add-ons are in), but the wording differs and is flagged for the source check.

**The most natural wrong answer — "she asked only about the hold, so only release the hold" — is
excluded by reasoning from visible sentences and records.** Doing only that leaves the governed result
in a state the visible principles do not allow: the release document's own sentence says what goes
back is **worked out only after** the money collected stands against the charges raised, and the
ledger shows 65.00 USD uncollected; further, the counter figure that produces that money is itself
**fixed only after** every finding carries its amount and the account carries the late-hand-in fee,
and the ledger shows a nil finding and no fee. A release computed on today's record would take the
agreement's owed figure as 65.00 USD and give back a different number, contradicting three sentences
that each stand in the document of the result they govern. Nothing had to be routed for me to see
this: each sentence names a **state**, and I found the write that brings the state about by searching
the corpus for the same words the records use.

**The fall-back answers — the computation documents alone, no factor applied — are computable,
definite, and different:**

| quantity | baseline-only figure | working, from the computation document and the product figures it names |
| --- | --- | --- |
| late hand-in fee | **408.00 USD** | stretch 2027-02-01…02-06 = 6 days, none set aside, Demo daily late fee 68.00 USD, 6 × 68.00, below the 1650.00 USD ceiling |
| damage finding | **41.25 USD** | 10 % of 1650.00 = 165.00, nothing set aside twice, whole carried, 25 % cover = 41.25 |
| counter settlement | **514.25 USD** | (440.50 + 408.00 + 41.25) − 375.50, nothing set against, written off or left standing |
| hold release | **650.00 USD**, `released` | owes (440.50 + 408.00 + 41.25) − (375.50 + 514.25) = 0.00; nothing moved or met; ×100 %; nothing released back; 650.00 − 0.00 |

Every factor document above was reached from words the **records** themselves use — `requested_due_date`
on a rental service request; `departure_date` on a lodging reservation; `reserved_date` against
`pickup_date`; `status='active'` and `passes_scan` rows on a season pass; a `rentals_deposit_hold` of
650.00 USD; `rentals_day_consume` rows; `swap_count` and `item_serial`; a `delivery_fee` charge; a
`damage_waiver` charge with `quantity=4`; `lessons_session_deliver` rows; a `passes_credit_issue` row;
`installment_balance_usd`; `folio_balance_usd` and `status='checked_out'`; `covered_holding_id` and
`benefit_remaining_usd`; `returned_date` and the count of `rentals_payment` rows. **No factor document
had to be guessed at**, and **no computation document told me a variation existed**: each of the four
computation documents states its baseline flatly ("Nothing is set aside …", "The daily figure is taken
in full …", "No passholder share is taken off"), with no "unless otherwise provided", no exception
list and no pointer.

### The one divergence, and what causes it

**Symptom.** Two of the four scored figures came out high: the late hand-in fee at 249.08 USD against
219.19 USD, and the counter settlement at 150.08 USD against 120.19 USD. Every tier selection, every
input count, every date, the whole problem tree, the tool sequence, the owners and the terminal state
are identical; the two figures differ only in how the **55 per cent standing share and the 20 per cent
exposure uplift are combined into one daily figure**.

**Root cause.** The computation document *Working Out the Shop's Fee for Late-Returned Equipment
Rental and Demo Kit* says:

> "The share and the uplift act on the daily figure itself rather than on one another's results, and
> neither is rounded before the fee is worked out."

That sentence is carried **verbatim** from `rentals_ext_late_handin_fee.baseline.rule` — the
rendering is faithful. But the sentence does not determine the arithmetic, and the structured
source's own `compute` takes the other branch:

> `result: "RND(MN(billable_days * daily_figure * standing_share * exposure_uplift, P('replacement_value_usd')), 2)"`

i.e. a straight product, 110.70 × 0.55 × 1.20 = 73.062 a day. I read "acts on the daily figure itself
rather than on one another's results" as denying exactly that composition — each adjustment measured
against the daily figure and its own movement then applied, 110.70 × (0.55 + 0.20) = 83.025 a day.
Under a product the uplift *is* worked out on what the share left, which is what the sentence says
does not happen.

**Why the visible corpus does not settle it.** I calibrated on the one document in the corpus that
states the same form of words and can be checked: *The Figure the Counter Asks For on an Equipment
Rental and Demo Agreement* says "The credit set against what is taken, the allowance written off and
the amount left standing against the hold are each taken off the figure the counter step arrived at,
and **none of them acts on another's result**", and there — three absolute amounts — the composition
really is non-compounding, each measured against the same base. The same form of words therefore
carries two different arithmetics in this corpus, and **no document anywhere in the 68 works an
example in which two non-baseline multipliers meet**: the late-fee, extension and change-fee
computation documents each run their worked example at the baseline, and each factor document shows
its own adjustment acting on a fresh figure. A reader has nothing to disambiguate against.

**Knock-on.** The 29.89 USD difference in the fee flows straight into the counter figure (280.19
against 310.08 at the counter step, 120.19 against 150.08 after the three take-offs) and then
cancels: what the agreement still owes after the payment is **225.00 USD on either reading**, because
the counter takes exactly the fee and the assessment less a fixed 160.00 USD, so the hold release
comes out at **628.00 USD** and `partially_forfeited` either way. The damage assessment, whose
computation document contains no such phrase, matched exactly at 61.00 USD.

**Fall-back column.** My baseline-only figures for the late fee (408.00) and the damage finding
(41.25) match `baseline_result` exactly. My counter fall-back of 514.25 USD and hold fall-back of
650.00 USD were computed by stacking *all four* baselines together; the source's `baseline_result`
figures (345.19 and 425.00) hold the other three policies' scored results fixed and strip only the
policy's own factors, which is a different quantity. That is a difference of convention in how the
fall-back is posed, not a disagreement about what either document says.

### Verdict

**KB-RUNTIME RED** for task 0.

The visible corpus supports two equally reasonable formulas for combining a share and an uplift that
"act on the daily figure itself rather than on one another's results", and the branch I derived from
it does not equal the source-layer solution for `late_fee_amount_usd` or `payment_amount_usd`.

Affected documents and locations:
- `env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/docs/rentals/late_handin_fee_computation_e5c4c325.json`, section
  "The quantity to be arrived at", the sentence beginning "The share and the uplift act on the daily
  figure itself…" — and the worked example below it, which never exercises the case.
- The same wording, unexercised, in
  `env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/docs/rentals/extension_charge_computation_580a1261.json` ("The resident
  share and the notice share act on the daily figure itself rather than on one another's results")
  and `env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/docs/rentals/model_change_fee_computation_7eea0595.json` ("The window
  share, the instruction share and the uplift each act on the package's change fee itself rather than
  on one another's results").
- The contrasting, genuinely non-compounding use of the same form of words in
  `env/env_0004_ski_resort_operator/docs/rentals/counter_settlement_computation_bc3589b7.json`, "Points of
  judgement → Where the three meet the figure".

**Nature of the root cause, stated honestly:** this is a **policy-side** defect. The sentence is
`rentals_ext_late_handin_fee.baseline.rule` verbatim, and the rendering carried it without change;
what disagrees with it is that policy's own `compute` expression. The same disagreement stands in
`rentals_ext_extension_charge` and `rentals_ext_model_change_fee`. It is reported here as required and
is not a reason to re-judge the documents, but it is also the reason the runtime part of this audit
cannot pass: a corpus that faithfully carries an underdetermined sentence is still a corpus a solver
cannot close.

Everything else on this task — the problem tree the customer never mentioned, every hop of it, every
tier, every date, the ordering, the owners and the terminal state — was derivable from the visible
materials alone and matched the source layer exactly.
